note: Applicability mirrors the *fullest* Guild dependency each agent has, using the same appliesTo vocabulary as guilds/manifest.json (web-app | api | cli | script). An agent listed under a type still runs for that type even when one of its consulted Guilds is conditional and doesn't apply — see each agent's own template for the conditional-consultation logic. quartermaster is the one agent narrowed at the manifest level rather than left to skip a Guild internally, since steps 10-11 have nothing to do at all for cli/script (no deploy target exists to route work to).
conditionalGuildsFormat: Two distinct kinds of condition, kept in separate fields on purpose: 'conditionalByType' is a Quest-type array, in the same appliesTo vocabulary as guilds/manifest.json's own field, and is safe for a CLI to parse and act on mechanically (the same way guilds/manifest.json's appliesTo already is, per bin/cli.js's selectGuilds). 'conditionalByContent' is a free-text note describing a condition that depends on this specific Quest's content (does it have a database, did an incident actually happen) rather than its declared type — it cannot be resolved from docs/quest-brief.md's Type field alone, so it is informational only. No tooling should branch on conditionalByContent the way bin/cli.js's cmdInit branches on appliesTo; it exists so a human or an agent reading this manifest understands why a guild is listed for an agent without being unconditionally required.

conditionalByContent.data: only when the Quest has a database, per docs/architecture.md — not derivable from Type alone
conditionalByContent.documentation: only the Post-incident documentation rule, and only when step 11 actually surfaces a real incident
